content_voiceover: This slide details the most frequent adverse events from ASCEMBL, comparing asciminib to bosutinib. On the left, hematologic and hepatic toxicities. Thrombocytopenia occurred in about thirty percent of asciminib patients versus twenty percent on bosutinib, with grade three or higher thrombocytopenia notably more common with asciminib, twenty two percent versus nine percent. Neutropenia rates were similar between arms. Hypertension was more frequent with asciminib. In contrast, bosutinib caused far more gastrointestinal and hepatic toxicity, diarrhea in seventy two percent of bosutinib patients versus just thirteen percent with asciminib, along with more nausea, vomiting, rash, and ALT elevation. So the toxicity profiles diverge, asciminib favors cytopenias and hypertension, bosutinib favors GI and liver effects. On the right, arterial occlusive events, a known class effect of concern with second and third generation TKIs. Asciminib showed a numerically higher rate of AOEs, five percent versus one percent with bosutinib, including myocardial ischemia, coronary artery disease, and ischemic stroke, translating to an exposure adjusted rate of about three per one hundred patient years versus roughly one and a half for bosutinib. This is an important safety signal fellows should recognize, since arterial thrombosis risk is a class effect that clinicians must monitor across all TKIs, including newer agents like asciminib.
keypoints: Asciminib caused more thrombocytopenia and hypertension than bosutinib
Bosutinib caused far more diarrhea, nausea, rash, and ALT elevation
Arterial occlusive events were higher with asciminib, about five percent versus one percent
Exposure adjusted AOE rate roughly three versus one and a half per hundred patient years
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the toxicity split, asciminib tends toward cytopenias, hypertension, and a higher arterial occlusive event rate, while bosutinib is dominated by gastrointestinal and hepatic side effects like diarrhea and transaminitis. The arterial occlusive event signal with asciminib is a key safety point to retain, since vascular monitoring matters across TKI classes.
